extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting full-length adult romance or women's fiction manuscripts to the All Love, All Voices Contest (particularly authors from diverse backgrounds / #ownvoices)
extracted.subtask_short: All Love All Voices contest submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting a full-length adult romance or women's fiction manuscript (plus required materials) to the Hachette Forever 'All Love, All Voices' contest, meeting all format, eligibility, and judging criteria. Includes following genre guidance (POV, tropes) and the contest's submission/format requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: 30% — Delineation of characters is well thought out and characters themselves are interesting, appealing, and relatable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion is weighted at 30% of judging. Judges will evaluate how well characters are drawn, their appeal, and relatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: 30% — An engaging story that features diverse characters with diverse backgrounds and diverse experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion is weighted at 30% of judging. Emphasis is on engagement and authentic, diverse characterization and experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: 20% — Dialogue in the Submission is clear, sufficient and presented in a believable, authentic and accurate manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 20%. Judges will assess clarity, sufficiency, believability, authenticity, and accuracy of dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: 20% — The Submission is grammatically correct and entrant understands basics of syntax and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 20%. Basic grammatical correctness, syntax, and punctuation are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre and manuscript type
rubrics_metrics.description: Be a full-length manuscript for a novel in one of the following two genres plus a 5 page synopsis: adult romance (focuses on characters meeting, getting to know each other and overcoming obstacles for their happily ever after); OR women's fiction (focuses on a woman’s journey and life experiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrant must choose either adult romance or women's fiction. Submission must include the manuscript plus a five-page synopsis. See separate entries for more detailed genre guidance (POV, tropes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity / #ownvoices
rubrics_metrics.description: Be reflective of diverse backgrounds and experiences, with an emphasis on #ownvoices, a hashtag associated with the movement supporting books about diverse characters written by authors from that same diverse group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: #OwnVoices stories are welcome and encouraged; contest is specifically seeking submissions from authors with diverse backgrounds who are promoting diversity in their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, content format, and word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Consist of text only in English, specifically between 75,000 - 95,000 words and should not include any photos, illustrations or names of real people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts must be plain text in English and fall within the stated word-count window; inclusion of images or real people's names is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a cover letter consisting of entrant’s name and the manuscript’s title and word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter must accompany the digital upload and include at minimum entrant name, manuscript title, and word count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-page synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 5-page synopsis detailing the plot, character, and relationship arcs in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synopsis must be five pages and explicitly detail plot progression, character development, and relationship arcs; this is required in addition to the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Be entrant’s original work and shall not consist of any third party created, owned copyrighted and/or trademarked material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be the entrant's original creation; do not include material owned or created by others, copyrighted/trademarked content, or third-party material.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format, filename, and submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: Be submitted as one digital upload in Microsoft Word format only via the Entry Form with the following file name format: [Manuscript Title]_[Entrant’s Last Name]. (Note: Sponsor will not accept hard copy or email submissions sent outside of the Entry Form.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single Word document uploaded through the official entry form only. Use exact filename format requested; submissions via hard copy or email will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women's fiction: focus and POV
rubrics_metrics.description: In women’s fiction, the focus will be on a woman’s journey and life experiences. Often these books center on female friendships, sisters, or discovering family secrets, told from the woman’s point of view. The narrative can either be in first person or third person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use first- or third-person POV focused on a woman's personal journey; examples of common subject matter include female friendships, sisters, or family secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romance: definition, POV, and common tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: For romance, the contest seeks a celebration of falling in love—characters who get to know each other, overcome obstacles, and then have a resolution that gives us all the warm, fuzzies of a happily-ever-after at the end. Often, there are dual, third-person points of view from each of the main protagonists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful romances often draw from popular tropes such as second-chance romance, friends-to-lovers, forbidden love (e.g., Romeo & Juliet), secret baby, marriage of convenience, fake engagement/significant other, or Cinderella (royals and billionaires). Dual third-person POVs are common but not mandatory.
